guard: a hermes platform that reconnects actually carries mesh traffic again, rather than reporting connected while receiving nothing
why: THIS CONFIG EXISTS BECAUSE THE SUITE IT GRADES WAS ADDED TO FIX A FALSE GREEN, AND A GUARD THAT
REPLACES A FALSE GREEN MUST ITSELF BE PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, or the same mistake has simply moved.
The history is worth keeping, because it is the whole argument for asserting effects. The first
version of this fix was guarded by `adapter-contract.smoke.ts`, which inspects the SIGNATURE of
CotalAdapter.connect and the PRESENCE of BridgeClient.reopen. Two reviewers independently
deleted the `if is_reconnect: reopen()` call and emptied reopen()'s body, and that suite stayed
green under BOTH, printing a confident `cells=23 passed=23 failed=0`. It could not have done
otherwise: a name and a signature do not change when a body is replaced by `return`. Adding more
cells of the same kind would have grown the tally and not the guard.
M1 EMPTIES reopen()'s BODY. This is the mutation that survived the signature suite verbatim.
The method still exists, is still called, and still has the right signature, so adapter-contract
remains green under it. The effect suite must redden, because with a latched stop event and a
dead reader the client never redials and no mesh message reaches a turn.
M2 DELETES THE CALL SITE. The near neighbour: reopen() is present and perfectly correct, the
adapter just never calls it on the reconnect path. One line from the subject, and the exact
defect the issue reports. Naming both is what distinguishes 'the method exists' from 'the
method runs and does something'.
M3 REMOVES THE BOUNDED JOIN, and it is the subtlest of the three. A reader that is still
clearing _stop leaves a window: a reader alive at the check that then reaches the top of its
loop and exits on the still-set flag stays installed as _reader, which rebuilds the dead bridge
the method exists to undo. It is timing dependent, so in production it surfaces as an occasional
silent platform rather than a clean failure. The suite forces that interleaving deterministically
instead of hoping to observe it, so this mutation reddens a named assertion every run.
NO BUILD STEP IS PREPENDED. The suite drives plugin/cotal/*.py through a real python3 against a
real Unix socket, so the interpreter reads the mutated source directly and the dist/ staleness
trap that forces `pnpm build` on the TypeScript mutations cannot apply.

mutations.name: M1 reopen() exists and is called but does nothing
mutations.find:
with self._lock:
            self._gen += 1
            reader = self._reader
            # Retire the old reader unconditionally: it belongs to a previous generation, so it is
            # not the active handle regardless of whether it has finished unwinding yet.
            self._reader = None
            # AND DROP THE SOCKET, which retiring the generation alone does not do. A retired
            # reader is almost always parked in `recv` on this very socket, and a generation check
            # cannot reach a thread blocked in a syscall: it is only evaluated at the TOP of the
            # loop, which the reader reaches after its recv returns. Leaving the socket installed
            # therefore leaves TWO readers on ONE socket, and the next frame is split between them
            # -- the retired one takes a chunk, sees its generation is stale, and exits carrying
            # those bytes, while the installed reader is left holding a fragment that never
            # completes a line. Small frames hide this because they fit in a single recv and so
            # cannot tear. Measured at 100KB before this close: 6 of 8 frames lost, two readers
            # alive on one socket every rep.
            #
            # Shutting down here makes the retirement reach the syscall. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS
            # COMMENT CLAIMED `close()` ALONE DID THAT, AND IT WAS WRONG: `close()` drops this
            # object's reference to the open file description, but a thread already blocked in
            # `recv` holds its own, so the description stays open and that read never returns. The
            # delivery cells could not catch the error because a reader stranded forever on a dead
            # socket stops competing for the new one just as well as a reader that exits, so the
            # frames arrived either way and the only trace was a leaked thread per reconnect.
            # `shutdown` acts on the connection rather than the descriptor, so the parked recv
            # returns at once, the retired reader exits without consuming a partial frame, and the
            # replacement dials a socket of its own.
            sock = self._sock
            self._sock = None
        if sock is not None:
            # SHUTDOWN BEFORE CLOSE, because `close()` alone does NOT wake a thread already blocked
            # in `recv` on this socket. `close()` drops THIS object's reference to the file
            # description; the blocked thread still holds its own, so the description stays open and
            # the read never returns. Measured directly on a socketpair: with `close()` alone the
            # reader was still blocked after 3s, and with `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)` first it returned
            # 0 bytes in 300ms. `shutdown` acts on the connection rather than the descriptor, so it
            # reaches the parked reader.
            #
            # This was a real leak, not a theoretical one: each retired reader stayed parked forever
            # on a socket nobody would ever write to, so every reconnect stranded one more thread.
            # Measured over 6 reopen cycles: bridge threads 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 without the shutdown and
            # flat at 1 with it. The delivery cell could not see this, because a reader stuck
            # forever on a dead socket stops competing for the new one just as effectively as a
            # reader that exits, so frames arrive either way.
            try:
                sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
            except OSError:
                pass  # already disconnected; the close below still frees the descriptor
            try:
                sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass

mutations.name: M2 the reconnect path never calls reopen()
mutations.find:
if is_reconnect:
            # Clear the latched stop and drop the dead reader, so start() below really starts one.
            #
            # OFF-LOOP, and that is not incidental. `reopen` joins the closed reader with a bounded
            # wait so a thread still unwinding is not mistaken for a live one, and a reader wedged
            # in a blocking recv makes that wait run to its full timeout. Calling it inline here
            # would stall the gateway's event loop for that whole period, freezing every other
            # platform in the process to repair this one. Measured at 2.00s against a wedged
            # reader, which is exactly the kind of pause an operator would report as the gateway
            # hanging on reconnect. `to_thread` keeps the loop free while the join runs.
            await asyncio.to_thread(self._client.reopen)
mutations.expectRed: AFTER A RECONNECT THE BRIDGE MUST STILL DELIVER: this is the silent dead-bridge defect from issue #1531
mutations.note: The defect exactly as reported. Note that connect() keeps its is_reconnect parameter under this mutation, so every signature assertion in adapter-contract stays green: this is the clearest demonstration that a signature test and an effect test are not substitutes. The find string is the whole is_reconnect block, since the call now runs through asyncio.to_thread and a one-line target went stale the moment that changed - the harness caught that as ERROR rather than reporting a false pass.

mutations.expectRed: AFTER A RECONNECT THE BRIDGE MUST STILL DELIVER: this is the silent dead-bridge defect from issue #1531
mutations.note: A HALF-APPLIED LATCH, which is the subtler failure and the reason this mutant is worth its own entry. The generation is bumped so _run stands down correctly, but the handle itself is never cleared, so start() still sees a non-None reader and creates no replacement. It isolates the retirement half of the fix from the stand-down half: a config that only restored the whole old body could not tell them apart. Measured: a half-applied latch is WORSE than none, because every reconnect leaves the stale handle installed rather than only the descheduled ones, so the headline delivery cell is what fires first. That is the honest name for this mutant and it is what expectRed records. The socket close reopen() performs is RETAINED in this mutant: without it the mutant would also reintroduce the M9 defect and the red could not be attributed to this mutation alone.

mutations.name: M4 the bounded join runs ON the gateway event loop
mutations.expectRed: the bounded join must run OFF the gateway event loop: a wedged reader must not freeze every other platform in the process
mutations.note: A REGRESSION THE BOUNDED JOIN ITSELF INTRODUCED, and it was found by measuring rather than reading: the inline call blocked the loop for a measured 2.00s against a wedged reader. Note that every OTHER cell in this suite stays green under this mutation, because the reconnect still delivers - it just freezes every other platform in the process while doing so. That is why the tick-count assertion exists rather than a timing threshold: both versions take the same 2.00s of wall time and only the loop's responsiveness during it differs.

mutations.expectRed: reopen must not leave a closed reader installed: a reader still unwinding when reopen is called must not be mistaken for a live one
mutations.note: THE DEAD HANDLE, restored. Three reviewers converged on this independently. A reader committed to exit but descheduled past the 2s window reads alive, stays installed, then dies, leaving a dead handle while the platform is marked connected and nothing ever looks again. Note the fast-unwind and live-reader control rows stay GREEN under this mutation, which is what makes the red attributable to the slow-unwind case rather than to reopen being broken in general. expectRed names the cell that fires FIRST under this mutant. Four cells go red together (retired-reader stand-down, slow-unwind retention, dead handle after exit, and live replacement), because they are four consequences of the same retained handle; the harness grades on the first, so it is the one named. The socket close reopen() performs is RETAINED in this mutant: without it the mutant would also reintroduce the M9 defect and the red could not be attributed to this mutation alone. expectRed re-derived from the assertion that actually fires first: the liveness mutant is caught by RACE_READER_CLEARED, which names this exact defect (a reader still unwinding mistaken for live), not by the two-readers-share-a-socket cell that fires later.

mutations.expectRed: connect() must return False and record a fatal when the bridge reader is dead, rather than reporting a connected platform that receives nothing
mutations.note: The second half of the fix, removed. Load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: verified against the pinned upstream source that the reconnect watcher iterates _failed_platforms only, entry requires a failed connect or a NOTIFIED retryable fatal, and there is no periodic health probe of a connected platform. Without this report a dead reader is never revisited and the bridge is deaf for the process lifetime. HEALTHY_READER_REPORTS_NO_FATAL stays green under it, so the cell is not merely asserting that connect always fails.

The fence in _connect still prevents a stale dialer INSTALLING over the live generation, so this mutant is invisible to M7's cells: what it restores is the READ. A reader retired while parked in _connect returns having installed nothing, finds the live generation's socket in _sock, and recv()s on it, stealing frames and dispatching them into a retired callback. Measured before the re-check: RETIRED_READER_READ_FOREIGN_SOCKET True.

mutations.name: M9 reopen retires the generation but leaves the socket installed
mutations.expectRed: a 100KB frame on the LAST subscriber must reach the installed reader on every rep
mutations.note: Retiring a generation does not reach a thread blocked in recv: the generation is only checked at the TOP of the loop, which a parked reader reaches after its recv returns. Leaving the socket installed therefore leaves two readers on one socket, and a frame larger than one recv(65536) is split between them: the retired reader takes a chunk and exits with it, leaving the installed reader holding a fragment that never completes a line. Invisible below 64KB because a small frame cannot tear. Measured at 100KB before this close: 6 of 8 lost, two readers alive every rep.

mutations.expectRed: a retired reader woken by EOF must not erase the live generation's socket, and a reply must still reach the broker
mutations.note: The EOF branch runs on OSError too, which is exactly how reopen wakes a retired reader. Without the identity check that reader erases the socket the LIVE generation installed, and _send then returns early on every outbound frame, so the seat is mute until an inbound wakes a redial. Measured with the guard removed: live socket installed 4 of 8, replies delivered 4 of 8, the four shape-A reps.

mutations.name: M11 reopen closes the socket without shutting it down first
mutations.expectRed: every reconnect must retire its reader thread rather than strand it in a blocked read
mutations.note: close() does not wake a thread already blocked in recv: it drops this object's reference to the open file description while the blocked thread keeps its own, so the read never returns. The delivery cells are blind to it because a reader stranded forever stops competing for the new socket just as well as one that exits. Measured: bridge threads grew 4,5,6,7,8,9,10 over six reopen cycles without the shutdown and stayed flat at 4 with it.

mutations.expectRed: a reader retired mid-dial must not install its socket over the live generation's: the lock makes the write atomic, not correct
mutations.note: MEASURED SURVIVOR, kept deliberately and disclosed rather than deleted. With only the pre-dial check removed the suite stays 52/52 green, because the under-lock check still refuses the clobber this probe constructs. That makes the pre-dial check an early-out rather than the correctness guard: it saves a pointless dial, and removing it costs work, not safety. A cell that kills this half would have to observe the dial NOT happening, which is a performance property, not a delivery one.

mutations.name: M7b the UNDER-LOCK generation check is removed (the pre-dial check remains)
mutations.expectRed: a dialer retired IN FLIGHT, past the pre-dial check, must not install its socket over the live generation's
mutations.note: The under-lock check is the correctness guard. A dialer parked past the pre-dial check and retired mid-dial is a window only this check covers; the mid-dial cell constructs exactly that, with MIDDIAL_PARK_REACHED proving the park was entered rather than skipped.
